key_insight: DecompRL learns to decompose hard coding tasks into modular sub-functions, making the search space easier so LLMs can solve problems that direct generation cannot.
engineering_relevance: It shifts inference cost from expensive GPU sampling to cheap CPU recombination and evaluation, cutting GPU token usage by about 50×.
method: Use reinforcement learning to train models to generate hierarchical code structures.
Split a problem into independently solvable modules, then implement each module separately.
Recombine k implementations across n modules to create up to k^n candidate solutions.
evidence_signal: On LiveCodeBench and CodeContests, DecompRL with Qwen 2.5 7B and Code World Model 32B outperformed standard and diversity-optimized RL baselines beyond 10^5 tokens per problem.
watch_item: The approach depends on the task being decomposable into verifiable sub-functions, so performance may drop when modular structure is unclear or module interfaces are hard to define.
paper_title: DecompRL: Solving Harder Problems by Learning Modular Code Generation
